title: Winged Bean (Sigarilyas): Characteristics
metaDescription: Winged Bean is an open pollinated winged bean variety from Allied Botanical. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Winged Bean is an open pollinated winged bean variety, also sold or known as Sigarilyas or Kalamismis. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Allied Botanical.

heroImage.alt: A farmer watering vegetable beds in Pulilan, Bulacan, the kind of farm where Winged Bean is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Sigarilyas or Kalamismis, this is the same winged bean. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [winged bean variety finder](/crop-varieties), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for legumes](/land-preparation/legume-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Days to harvest, by the seller's count: first harvest 105 to 110 days after transplanting. No trial on record checks this figure yet, so treat it as the seller's own and compare with farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit winged bean fields most often: [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot), [powdery mildew](/diseases/powdery-mildew), [legume pod borer](/pests/legume-pod-borer), [root knot nematode](/diseases/root-knot-nematode). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: the winged bean Allied Botanical sells, no registered winged bean varieties exist (the NSIC list has no winged bean sheet). These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual winged bean on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Winged Bean

Sigarilyas needs short days to flower well, so plant it in the second half of the year. Pick young, tender pods. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items.q: Is Sigarilyas the same as Winged Bean?
items.a: Yes. Sigarilyas is another name for Winged Bean. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
Yes. It is open pollinated, so seed from a clean, isolated field grows true. Still, certified seed gives the best start every few seasons.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Winged Bean?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
